name: waterdeep
lore: The City of Splendors, a massive metropolis on the Sword Coast.

subLocations.name: the lady dreaming
subLocations.lore:
History
During the Spellplague of 1385 DR, the walking statue appeared and rampaged through the city. When the statues were stopped, she fell onto her side, where she still lay by 1492 DR.[

Description
It resembled a noble woman asleep in a garden. She bore the appearance of a female elf and, while active, her clothing and hair appeared to move naturally

subLocations.name: Street of Lances
subLocations.lore: Street of Lances was walked by broadcryers who peddled their broadsheets to passers-by.

subLocations.name: Seawind Alley
subLocations.lore: Seawind Alley was an alley notable for the ghostly voices that could be heard within the alley.

subLocations.name: Ghostwalk
subLocations.lore: Ghostwalk was considered sufficiently safe for the rich inhabitants of the ward to walk by undisturbed. Like other alleys in the Sea Ward, it was clean and wide. It contained numerous shadowtops that were favored by children to climb and play by.

subLocations.name: Westwall Street
subLocations.lore: Westwall Street was located in the western section of Waterdeep's Sea Ward, fully spanning the entire western boundary of the ward with the exterior wall in that portion of the city.

subLocations.name: Heroes' Walk
subLocations.lore: Every year during the summer, Heroes' Garden and Heroes' Walk were both overtaken by the nobles of the Church of Siamorphe on their holy day, the Divine Pageantry.

subLocations.name: Heroes' Garden
subLocations.lore: Heroes' Garden was one of the only public gardens in the city besides the City of the Dead.

subLocations.name: Trollkill Street
subLocations.lore: Trollkill Street was a large road in the city of Waterdeep, spanning nearly the whole northern portion of the Trollwall, that started in the Sea Ward and ended in the North Ward.

subLocations.name: Street of the Singing Dolphin
subLocations.lore: The Street of the Singing Dolphin was located in the western section of Waterdeep's Sea Ward. The road spanned the entire western side of the ward

subLocations.name: Oar Alley
subLocations.lore: A minor avenue of hard-packed earth and [[gravel]] that extended off of [[Ship Street]] and terminated in a dead end.

subLocations.name: New Olamn
subLocations.lore: The College of New Olamn, simply known as New Olamn, was a traditional bardic college

subLocations.name: Sahuagin Humbled
subLocations.lore: The [[Walking Statue of Waterdeep]] known as the Sahuagin Humbled was originally the only Walking Statue visible in Waterdeep.

subLocations.name: Deepwater Harbor
subLocations.lore: Thanks to continuous efforts by the [[Guild of Watermen]] and its [[merfolk]] population, the cold waters of Deepwater Harbor were exceptionally clean.

subLocations.name: Deepwater Isle
subLocations.lore: Deepwater was the largest in a ring of islands that enclosed and protected [[Deepwater Harbor]].

subLocations.name: T'Quession
subLocations.lore: T'Quession was a [[sea elf]] hamlet.

subLocations.name: Naval Harbor
subLocations.lore: The fleet of Waterdeep's navy was based in the Naval Harbor. Commercial and personal vessels were not permitted in this area.

subLocations.name: Market
subLocations.lore: The largest open area within the city was the marketplace between Trader's Way and Bazaar street. It was full of merchants carts and stalls both day and night and was the best place in the city to find a good price for any trade good found in Faerûn, assuming one had some skill at haggling.

subLocations.name: Gull Leap
subLocations.lore: A cliff along the northwestern edge of Waterdeep, just outside the Trollwall, that was named in part for the significant amount of [[sea gull]]s that nested upon it.

subLocations.name: House of the Homeless
subLocations.lore:
The House of the Homeless was a large mausoleum.

The dead of Waterdeep were interred within the House of the Homeless if they died without laying claim, or payment, to any other burial site.

subLocations.name: Merchants' Rest
subLocations.lore: Merchants' Rest, which was also known as the Coinscoffin, was a tomb. Despite its name, Merchants' Rest was reserved for anyone, whether they were a merchant or not, who prepaid to be interred within.

subLocations.name: Hall of the Sages
subLocations.lore: The Hall of the Sages was a tomb. As its name implied, the Hall of the Sages was reserved specifically for [[sage]]s.

subLocations.name: Hall of Heroes
subLocations.lore:
The Hall of Heroes was a tomb. 

Blue [[marble]] was used for the tomb's walls. The interior was decorated with trophies of famous fallen warriors including the sword hilt of [[Raurlor]].

subLocations.name: Mariners' Rest
subLocations.lore: Mariners' Rest was a tomb. As its name implied, the tomb was reserved sailors and seamen who prepaid to be interred within.

subLocations.name: Deepwinter Vault
subLocations.lore: The Deepwinter Vault was a mausoleum that belonged to the defunct noble [[Deepwinter (family) |Deepwinter]] family. It was also one of the entrances to the former lair of [[Artor Morlin]], the [[vampire lord]] of Waterdeep.

subLocations.name: Roads' End
subLocations.lore: The tomb was used as a communal burial site for travelers who perished while visiting the City of Splendors.

subLocations.name: Sultlue Vault
subLocations.lore: The tomb was heavily warded with magic.

subLocations.name: Lords' Respite
subLocations.lore: The Lords' Respite was reserved for any Lords of Waterdeep who wished to be buried there.

subLocations.name: Trollwall
subLocations.lore: The Trollwall was a defensive barrier that encircled nearly the entirety of the city of Waterdeep.

subLocations.name: Trollfort
subLocations.lore: This structure stood four stories tall and was directly connected to the city walls that surrounded the Field Ward.

subLocations.name: North Tower
subLocations.lore: The North Tower, also known as the Trolltower, was a torchtower. It had all the features that were common among them. This included a debriefing room, a small armory, holding cells, storage rooms for the holding of evidence or confiscated items, some bedchambers, and some garderobes.

subLocations.name: Dock Ward
subLocations.lore: The Dock Ward of Waterdeep was situated on the Great Harbor of Waterdeep. It contained the docks, shipbuilding yards, and warehouses for the sea trade. Compared to the rest of the city it was exceptionally dirty, smelly, and particularly dangerous.

subLocations.name: Southern Ward
subLocations.lore: Southern Ward was the southeastern sector of the city of Waterdeep.

subLocations.name: Trades Ward
subLocations.lore: The Trades Ward was one of the seven wards of the city of Waterdeep. It was the main shopping district of Waterdeep and housed many of the city's guildhalls.

subLocations.name: Castle Ward
subLocations.lore: The Castle Ward was the central ward of the city of Waterdeep.

subLocations.name: City of the Dead
subLocations.lore: The City of the Dead was a large cemetery and ward in Waterdeep. Most of the city's dead were buried here. By day, it also doubled as the city's major public park picnic area.

subLocations.name: North Ward
subLocations.lore: The North Ward was the northeastern sector of Waterdeep. It was famous for being the quietest ward of the city, consisting mostly of residential areas.

subLocations.name: Sea Ward
subLocations.lore: The Sea Ward of Waterdeep was the wealthiest ward in Waterdeep and located in the northwest of the city.

subLocations.name: Field Ward
subLocations.lore: The Field Ward of Waterdeep was an unofficial ward of the city, located between the inner and outer walls on the north side of town. It was in fact the city's slums — possessing the poorest living conditions within the city.

subLocations.name: Undercliff
subLocations.lore: Undercliff was a rural community just outside the walls of Waterdeep, located east of the city proper. Along with the Field Ward, it was considered an unofficial ward of the city.

subLocations.name: Eirontalar Villa
subLocations.lore: A second [[Eirontalar Villa]].

subLocations.name: Trollskull Manor
subLocations.lore: Four stories tall and boasting balconies, a turret, and five chimneys, the abandoned building is one of the grandest in Trollskull Alley.

subLocations.name: House of Inspired Hands
subLocations.lore: The House of Inspired Hands was a temple of [[Gond]].

subLocations.name: House of Heroes
subLocations.lore: The House of Heroes was a temple dedicated to the god [[Tempus]], the Lord of Battles. It was one of the biggest temples in Waterdeep.

subLocations.name: House of the Moon
subLocations.lore: The House of the Moon was a temple of [[Selûne]]. It was one of the largest temples in the city.

subLocations.name: Shrine of Silvanus
subLocations.lore: The Shrines of Nature was a temple complex in Waterdeep dedicated to the worship of the deities Mielikki and Silvanus, as well as a garden. The shrine dedicated to Silvanus was known by many names, including Seatrees Shrine, the Green Garden, the Quiet Place, and Oakenshade House.

subLocations.name: The Lady's Hands
subLocations.lore: The Shrines of Nature was a temple complex in Waterdeep dedicated to the worship of the deities Mielikki and Silvanus, as well as a garden. The shrine dedicated to Mielikki was commonly known as the Lady's Hand.

subLocations.name: Tower of Luck
subLocations.lore: The Tower of Luck was a temple of [[Tymora]].

subLocations.name: Temple of Beauty
subLocations.lore: The Temple of Beauty was a temple of [[Sune]].

subLocations.name: House of Wonder
subLocations.lore: The House of Wonder was a mage academy and temple of [[Mystra]].

subLocations.name: Plinth
subLocations.lore: The Plinth was a temple for all faiths and was the only temple located in the [[Trades Ward]].

subLocations.name: Halls of Justice
subLocations.lore: The Halls of Justice was a temple of [[Tyr]].

subLocations.name: Font of Knowledge

subLocations.name: Hospice of St. Laupsenn
subLocations.lore: The Hospice of St. Laupsenn was a temple of [[Ilmater]].

subLocations.name: Monastery of the Sun
subLocations.lore: Monastery of the Sun was a [[monastery]] dedicated to [[Amaunator]]

subLocations.name: House of Two Hands
subLocations.lore: The House of Two Hands was a monastery belonging to the [[Order of the Even-Handed]].

subLocations.name: Temple of Good Cheer
subLocations.lore: The Temple of Good Cheer was a makeshift temple dedicated to [[Lliira]] and [[Milil]].

subLocations.name: Helm's Hall
subLocations.lore: Helm's Hall was a temple dedicated to [[Helm]].

subLocations.name: Sailor's Last Request
subLocations.lore: The Sailor's Last Request was a small chapel to [[Valkur]], built in an old and small warehouse.

subLocations.name: Holyhands House
subLocations.lore:
Holyhands House was a temple to all deities.

This temple was once a villa that belonged to the [[Maernos]] noble family and was a bequeathal by the last of the Maernos line, [[Ultas Maernos]].

subLocations.name: gralkyn's tavern
subLocations.lore:
History
During the Spellplague of 1385 DR, the walking statue appeared and rampaged through the city. When stopped, the statue tumbled backwards onto a building.

Gralkyn's Tavern sat in the statue's lap by 1492 

Description
The pose resembled that of a drunkard who had fallen asleep, its arms limp to the sides and its head tilted on its chest. The statue originally carried a large stone battleaxe, which was located nearby in the cobbles where it fell.

subLocations.name: Endshift Tavern
subLocations.lore: The Endshift Tavern was a frequent stop for off-duty members of the [[City Guard (Waterdeep)|City Guard]].

subLocations.name: The Ship's Wheel
subLocations.lore: The Ship's Wheel had a reputation for being one of the safest taverns around. Most activity within the tavern never got more exciting than the old patrons watching each others hair fall out.

subLocations.name: The Pilgrim's Rest
subLocations.lore: This comfortable inn was moderately priced, at least by Waterdeep standards. Many of the patrons stayed here while visiting Waterdeep's temples. A private room could be had for 9 gp per night and included stabling and a meal.

subLocations.name: The Wandering Wemic
subLocations.lore: Rooms could be had at the Wandering Wemic at a rate of 10 gp per night and included stabling, a valet service used for cleaning or repairing gear, and one bottle of wine per person per evening.

subLocations.name: Fiery Flagon
subLocations.lore: The Fiery Flagon was a stately old tavern that served excellent food.

subLocations.name: The Sleeping Snake
subLocations.lore: Rowdy tavern for dockhands and dancers, owner by [[Alard Belaerl]].

subLocations.name: Shipmasters' Hall
subLocations.lore: Shipmasters' Hall was an inn.

subLocations.name: Selûne's Smile
subLocations.lore: Selûne's Smile, also known as the Inn of the Crescent Moon, was a tavern and inn devoted to [[Selûne]]. Uniquely, it was established and run by an [[avatar]] of the goddess Selûne.

subLocations.name: The Red Gauntlet
subLocations.lore: Food served here consisted mostly of dried fish, waybread, and rabbit-and-fowl stew. Drink consisted of a house wine. The fares were cheap in the Red Gauntlet with a plate of food running just 3 cp and a tankard 2 cp.

subLocations.name: Copper Cup
subLocations.lore: The Copper Cup was a [[festhall]].

subLocations.name: Yawning Portal
subLocations.lore: The Yawning Portal inn gained most of its renown for being the primary open route to the [[Undermountain]].

subLocations.name: Bowels of the Earth
subLocations.lore: The tavern was a well-known spot for hiring [[mercenaries]].

subLocations.name: Rearing Hippocampus
subLocations.lore: The Rearing Hippocampus was an inn.

subLocations.name: The Blackstar Inn
subLocations.lore: The Blackstar Inn was owned by [[Asiyra Boldwinter]] during the mid-to-late 14th century DR. Armed guards protected the entryway and the stables.

subLocations.name: Gray Serpent
subLocations.lore: The Gray Serpent, which was also seen as the Grey Serpent, was an inn located in Waterdeep during the mid-to-late 14th century DR.

subLocations.name: Swords' Rest
subLocations.lore: Swords' Rest was a tavern and a good place to hire [[mercenaries]].

subLocations.name: Felzoun's Folly
subLocations.lore: This tavern was frequently quite crowded and noisy, but overall was a casual place where merchants and consumers alike stopped for a quick bite or drink.

subLocations.name: Ship's Prow
subLocations.lore: The inn's name derived from the fact that it was converted into a building from the prow of a ship.

subLocations.name: The Mermaid's Arms
subLocations.lore: The Mermaid's Arms was a pricey and busy tavern, inn, and festhall.

subLocations.name: Blue Mermaid
subLocations.lore: The tavern was well appointed and clean, if a bit tired.

subLocations.name: Hanging Lantern
subLocations.lore: The Hanging Lantern was a [[festhall]]. The building stood an impressive six storys tall.

subLocations.name: Sleeping Wench
subLocations.lore: This tavern could be rather rowdy, but less so compared to the [[Sleeping Snake]] and had a comparably better clientele.

subLocations.name: Thirsty Sailor
subLocations.lore: The Thirsty Sailor was an infamous dive bar.

subLocations.name: Warm Beds
subLocations.lore: Warm Beds was an [[inn]].

subLocations.name: Bloody Fist
subLocations.lore: The Bloody Fist was a [[tavern]].

subLocations.name: Hanged Man
subLocations.lore: This tavern offered a fine selection of [[wine]]s, far better than one might suspect it to have, as well as a wide variety of [[ale]]s.

subLocations.name: Three Pearls Nightclub
subLocations.lore: The Three Pearls Nightclub was a [[festhall]] and nightclub.

subLocations.name: Purple Palace
subLocations.lore: The Purple Palace was a [[festhall]].

subLocations.name: Thirsty Throat
subLocations.lore: The Thirsty Throat was a [[tavern]].

subLocations.name: Blushing Mermaid
subLocations.lore: The Blushing Mermaid was a tavern, inn, and festhall managed by Lady [[Alathene Moonstar]] circa the Year of Wild Magic, [[1372 DR]].

subLocations.name: Jade Dancer
subLocations.lore: The Jade Dancer was a [[festhall]] and [[tavern]].

subLocations.name: The Full Cup
subLocations.lore: The Full Cup's patrons were mostly caravan drovers. Brawls were a common occurrence in this seedy [[tavern]].

subLocations.name: Pampered Traveler
subLocations.lore: Pampered Traveler was a fine establishment with large, well-furnished rooms, a play area for children, and a library that guests could peruse.

subLocations.name: Inn of the Dripping Dagger
subLocations.lore: The Inn of the Dripping Dagger was the favored bar and home to many adventurers, mercenaries, misfits and soldiers.

subLocations.name: Mother Tathlorn's House of Pleasure and Healing
subLocations.lore: Mother Tathlorn's House of Pleasure and Healing was a festhall and spa.
grounding: https://forgottenrealms.fandom.com/wiki/Mother Tathlorn's House of Pleasure and Healing

subLocations.name: Elfstone Tavern
subLocations.lore: The Elfstone Tavern was a tavern. It catered to elves and half-elves in the city.

subLocations.name: Golden Horn Gambling House
subLocations.lore: The Golden Horn Gambling House, which was also simply called the Golden Horn, was a [[festhall]].

subLocations.name: Unicorn's Horn
subLocations.lore: The Unicorn's Horn was an [[inn]].

subLocations.name: Gondalim's
subLocations.lore: Gondalim's was an [[inn]].

subLocations.name: Gentle Rest
subLocations.lore: The Gentle Rest was an [[inn]].

subLocations.name: The Gentle Mermaid
subLocations.lore: The Gentle Mermaid was a tavern, festhall, and gambling hall. The Gentle Mermaid had the largest gambling room throughout Waterdeep, and perhaps even throughout [[Faerûn]].

subLocations.name: The Raging Lion
subLocations.lore: The Raging Lion was owned by a man named [[Lhaerhlin Masram]]. Several [[dwarves]] and female [[adventurer]]s used the inn as their home. They helped Lhaerhlin maintain order during their stays between outings.

subLocations.name: A Maiden's Tears
subLocations.lore: A Maiden's Tears, which was also simply called the Tears, was a tavern. The tavern was quiet compared to others located in this part of the North Ward and patrons appreciated its private booths.

subLocations.name: The Misty Beard
subLocations.lore: Part of what made the Misty Beard famous up and down the [[Sword Coast]] was the staff which was composed of exotic or monstrous creatures from all over [[Faerûn]].

subLocations.name: Galloping Minotaur
subLocations.lore: Galloping Minotaur was an [[inn]] that was widely known and frequented by merchants and travelers.

subLocations.name: The Sailors' Own
subLocations.lore: The Sailors' Own was a rather shabby tavern near the docks.

subLocations.name: Crawling Spider
subLocations.lore: The Crawling Spider was a [[tavern]]. The tavern had a mock underground decor made from plaster and rock rubble. Stuffed spiders hung from the ceiling, giving the tavern its namesake.

subLocations.name: Sated Satyr
subLocations.lore: The Sated Satyr was a two-story, irregularly shaped building that fronted the streets or the alley on all sides but one.

subLocations.name: Wyvern's Rest
subLocations.lore: The Wyvern's Rest was an inn. Originally constructed as a stone watch house, the Wyvern's Rest was a favorite of guards and watchmen.

subLocations.name: Golden Harp Inn
subLocations.lore: The Golden Harp Inn was an [[inn]].

subLocations.name: High Flagon
subLocations.lore: The High Flagon was a gambling hall and inn.

subLocations.name: Twilight Hunters
subLocations.lore: Twilight Hunters was a tavern.

subLocations.name: Sapphire House
subLocations.lore: Sapphire House was an expensive rooming house.

subLocations.name: Tavern of the Flagon Dragon
subLocations.lore: The Tavern of the Flagon Dragon was a tavern.

subLocations.name: Jhrual's Dance
subLocations.lore: Jhrual's Dance was a [[festhall]].

subLocations.name: Smiling Siren
subLocations.lore: The Smiling Siren was a bawdy tavern/nightclub and theater that later became a [[festhall]] run by the church of [[Sune]].

subLocations.name: Mighty Manticore
subLocations.lore: This tavern was known for its thick and flavorful stew, sharp [[cheese]], fresh black bread, and hearty ale.

subLocations.name: The Asp's Strike
subLocations.lore: The Asp's Strike was a [[tavern]].

subLocations.name: Grinning Lion
subLocations.lore: The Grinning Lion was a [[tavern]].

subLocations.name: Greenglade Tower
subLocations.lore: Greenglade Tower was a popular and rather clean rooming house.

subLocations.name: Maelstrom's Notch
subLocations.lore: The Maelstrom's Notch was an [[inn]].

subLocations.name: Pickled Fisherman
subLocations.lore: The Pickled Fisherman was a tavern.

subLocations.name: Soaring Pegasus
subLocations.lore: The Soaring Pegasus was a tavern.

subLocations.name: Angry Coxswain
subLocations.lore: A [[magical]] ''[[Angry Coxswain Portal|portal]]'' existed within the tavern that Ramas and Orth used to ferry slaves to [[Mulhorand]]. The portal connected directly to a prison cell located in a market in [[Skuld]].

subLocations.name: Singed Bolt
subLocations.lore: The Singed Bolt was a tavern.

subLocations.name: Blackstone House
subLocations.lore: Mercenaries could be hired at Blackstone House.

subLocations.name: Blushing Nymph
subLocations.lore: The Blushing Nymph, or just the Nymph, was a festhall.

subLocations.name: Underdark
subLocations.lore: The Underdark tavern had a secret passage that led to [[Undermountain]] in the back of the establishment's basement.

subLocations.name: The Splintered Stair
subLocations.lore: A large spiraling staircase overlooked by balconies dominated the entry of the inn. The stairway was badly damaged during an epic brawl between adventurers, giving the inn its name. The rooms for rent were large, but also dark and cold.

subLocations.name: The Spouting Fish
subLocations.lore: The Spouting Fish was a popular tavern.

subLocations.name: Madame Garah's Boarding House
subLocations.lore: Madame Garah's Boarding House was a row house used as a boarding house.

subLocations.name: Soaring Delights
subLocations.lore: Soaring Delights was a [[:category:restaurants|restaurant]] built on the first floor of the hollow [[Hawk Man]].

subLocations.name: Skewered Dragon
subLocations.lore: The Skewered Dragon was a tavern. The clientele was primarily made up of dock workers that were suspicious of strangers.

subLocations.name: Field of Triumph
subLocations.lore:
The Field of Triumph was a large outdoor stadium.

The Field of Triumph was the venue for many public spectacles from late spring until late autumn, weather permitting. The Open Lord of Waterdeep used the Field as a public forum to give proclamations to the city.

subLocations.name: Market Hall
subLocations.lore: Market Hall was the guildhall of the [[Council of Farmer-Grocers]].

subLocations.name: Watermens' Hall
subLocations.lore: Watermens' Hall was the guildhall of the [[Guild of Watermen]].

subLocations.name: Mariners' Hall
subLocations.lore: The Mariners' Hall was the guildhall of the [[Master Mariners' Guild]].

subLocations.name: League Hall
subLocations.lore: League Hall was the guildhall of the [[League of Skinners & Tanners]].

subLocations.name: Butchers' Guildhall
subLocations.lore: The Butchers' Guildhall was the headquarters of the [[Guild of Butchers]].

subLocations.name: Cookhouse Hall
subLocations.lore: Cookhouse Hall was a civic building.

subLocations.name: Bell Tower
subLocations.lore: A municipal bell tower that was used to signal the presence of fires, attacks on the city, or call for assemblies at [[Piergeiron's Palace]].

subLocations.name: Metal House of Wonders
subLocations.lore: Metal House of Wonders was the guildhall of the [[Splendid Order of Armorers, Locksmiths, and Finesmiths]].

subLocations.name: Stone House
subLocations.lore: The Stone House was the guildhall of the [[Carpenters', Roofers', & Plaisterers' Guild]].

subLocations.name: Cobblers' & Corvisers' House
subLocations.lore: The Cobblers' and Corvisers' House was the guildhall of the [[Order of Cobblers & Corvisers]].

subLocations.name: House of Good Spirits
subLocations.lore: The House of Good Spirits was the guildhall of the [[Vintners', Distillers', & Brewers' Guild]].

subLocations.name: Coach & Wagon Hall
subLocations.lore: The Coach & Wagon Hall was the headquarters of the [[Wagonmakers' and Coach Builders' Guild]].

subLocations.name: Saddlers' & Harness-Makers' Hall
subLocations.lore: The Saddlers' & Harness-Makers Hall, also known simply as the Saddlers' Hall, was the headquarters of the [[Saddlers' and Harness-makers' Guild]].

subLocations.name: Wheel Hall
subLocations.lore: Wheel Hall was the guildhall of the [[Weelwrights' Guild]].

subLocations.name: Shipwrights' House
subLocations.lore: Shipwrights' House was the guildhall of the [[Order of Master Shipwrights]].

subLocations.name: Full Sails
